title: On Fruitlessness, Shame, and False Sustenance
english: He is named as such from the beginning. He slaughtered his own victims and poured his own wine into a bowl. The same food and meat are named as bread and milk and vegetables and wine. However, the foolish are said to partake as if it were her bread and as if it were poured wine. If this is so, how shall we understand that 'man ate the bread of angels' (1 Cor 10:3)? Spiritual knowledge is a bowl containing discourses concerning the incorporeal and the corporeal and judgment and providence.

If Paul the apostle is a servant of Christ, and Christ is wisdom, then Paul the apostle is a servant of wisdom. Likewise, we shall gather the word concerning the rest of the apostles and the prophets, having shown them to be servants of wisdom. Calling with a high proclamation to the bowl, saying: This proclamation alone is a high place of knowledge proclaiming God.

He did not say 'eat of my meats'; for 'solid food is for the mature' (Heb 5:13). One must not rebuke the evil, so that they may not hate you. It is not necessary to rebuke the evil ones who are sinning, but rather to discourse with them concerning the fear of God, which persuades them to depart from wickedness.

If 'to know the law is the work of a good mind,' and to do the commandment is the work of a good mind. However, to do the commandment comes before knowing the law, if it is the nature of knowledge to come after purification.

He who relies on falsehoods, he will shepherd winds; and he himself will chase flying birds, being carried about by every wind of teaching and having shipwrecked concerning the faith. For he left the paths of his own vineyard; he has gone astray from the axes of his own farm. For he left the vine that said: 'I am the vine, you are the branches' (John 15:5), and: 'My father is the farmer' (John 15:1).

Fruitlessness brings about wickedness and ignorance by its own hands. A foolish and impudent woman becomes lacking in shame, one who does not know shame; since shame is a teacher, it is said 'she does not know shame.' And David says that the fear of God is a teacher: 'Come, children, listen to me, I will teach you the fear of the Lord' (Ps 138:14). But if fear and shame are natural passions of the soul, how are they teachers? Perhaps he calls the teaching about the fear of the Lord 'the fear of the Lord,' which teaches us that we must turn away from wickedness, as it is said, 'all shall turn from evil by the fear of the Lord' (Lk 6:27). Again, he calls 'shame' the discourses concerning repentance and shame that lead us to a sense of our own sins. Thus David says: 'I will behold the heavens, the works of your fingers, the moon and the stars which you established' (Ps 138:14), that is, I will behold the discourses concerning heavens, moon, and stars.

Seize the sweetness of hidden bread and the pleasantness of stolen water: 'Bread of lies will be sweet to them, and after this their mouth will be filled with pebbles' (Prov 9:17). But flee; do not linger in that place, nor fix your eye upon it. It is not necessary to linger the mind with worthless thoughts; 'for no one carries fire in his bosom and burns his clothes' (Lk 6:3). And do not drink from a foreign spring or a foreign well. Just as with God there is a spring of life, so with the devil there is a spring of death. If the spring of God is a spring of virtue and knowledge, then clearly the spring of the devil is a spring of wickedness and ignorance. Likewise, one must consider this regarding rivers, wells, waters, and rains.

Lawless treasures will not profit, but righteousness will rescue from death: 'Lawless treasures will not profit,' which they have stored up upon the earth, 'where moth and worm destroy, and where thieves break in and steal' (Matt 6:19).
